identifiabilityModel.observations: x=C_s(g) at generation and y=C_r(g+d) at receipt
identifiabilityModel.minimalCounterexample: Even with a_s=a_r=1, y-x=d+(b_r-b_s). Delay 20 ms with receiver offset 100 ms and delay 120 ms with offset 0 ms produce the same observed difference but opposite truth under a 50 ms deadline.

primaryTheory.title: Fundamentals of Large Sensor Networks: Connectivity, Capacity, Clocks, and Computation
primaryTheory.role: Clock offset and directed one-way delay are not jointly identified from the relevant timestamp observations.

primaryTheory.title: RFC 7679: A One-Way Delay Metric for IPPM
primaryTheory.role: One-way delay measurement requires synchronized source and destination clocks and explicit clock uncertainty and timestamping boundaries.

verifiedFieldContracts.finding: CPM provides a referenceTime and per-object measurementDeltaTime but not receiver clock identity, synchronization state, or mapping-error bounds.
TimestampIts uses an ITS epoch while CAM generationDeltaTime is modulo 65536; the numeric field alone does not prove a common sender and receiver time basis.

verifiedFieldContracts.source: SAE J2735 and USDOT BSM sample contract
verifiedFieldContracts.finding: BSM secMark is milliseconds within a minute and requires external minute and clock-source context for cross-host age.
Sidelink synchronization fields describe radio-frame synchronization references, not application capture, host receipt, or their error bounds.
ROS distinguishes System, Steady, and ROS time and permits jumps under simulated time, while the ordinary serialized Header does not carry clock type.
Messages carry log_time and publish_time, but publish_time may equal log_time when unavailable and the specification does not assign a clock-domain meaning.

PTP and generalized PTP expose domain, grandmaster, time-base changes, and asymmetry handling that can support provenance, but configuration presence does not bind every application timestamp to that state.

nearestWorkBoundary.occupiedSpace: AoI assumes generation and current time can be compared on a meaningful common axis.
Asynchronous feature compensation under comparable continuous timestamps.
Joint clock offset, skew, path-asymmetry, AoI, and fusion handling; a new synchronization or AoI-compensation model is not claimed here.
Time-aware provenance for distributed state, not a V2X field contract and one-way-age identified set.

noveltyBoundary: Audit each frozen V2X, ROS, or MCAP timestamp for event semantics, producer, clock domain, synchronization generation, timestamping plane, and mapping-error interval.
Compute an identified interval for capture-to-use age instead of introducing a new synchronization model or forcing a point estimate.
Return fresh, stale, or uncertain according to a deadline and explicitly refuse an unidentifiable verdict.
Separate sensor capture, feature ready, publish, wire transmit and receive, host receive, log, replay publish, fusion use, and inference finish.

intervalRule.definition: If sender and receiver events map to reference-time intervals [L_s(x),U_s(x)] and [L_r(y),U_r(y)], then A(x,y)=[L_r(y)-U_s(x), U_r(y)-L_s(x)] intersect [0,infinity).
decision: Upper bound at or below D means certainly fresh.
Lower bound above D means certainly stale.

openAssets.use: Audit log and publish times and available synchronization provenance; the public take audit does not establish an independent latency or sync-state channel.
Contrast image_timestamp, pointcloud_timestamp, and system_error_offset with missing clock-source and relock provenance.
Validate message and capture timestamp boundaries without assuming capture clocks are synchronized to senders.
Inject offset, drift, and relock while fixing the network process; a shared simulation clock is not treated as physical multi-host evidence.

twoWeekMinimum: Freeze standard versions, repository commits, one CooperScene take, and a synthetic ROS 2 MCAP; build a producer, event, clock-domain, and timestamping-plane ledger.
Construct observationally identical dual-world traces while preserving message content, order, and service process.
Inject offset 0, plus or minus 20, 100, and 500 ms; drift plus or minus 10, 50, and 100 ppm; one step or relock; and deadlines 50, 100, and 200 ms.
Implement a read-only replay age gate and compare naive subtraction, MCAP log-minus-publish, RTT over two, PTP point estimate, oracle common clock, and interval provenance.
Release the field ledger, counterexample pairs, identified-set calculator, sidecar schema, and reproducible manifest without training a perception model.
sixWeekStudy: Extend the field audit and sidecar to CooperScene, DAIR-V2X, NIST packet captures, and ROS 2 or MCAP.
Use linuxptp ptp4l and phc2sys to generate calibrated software synchronization states without generalizing them to automotive radio or hardware timestamping.
Insert the age gate before one runnable public cooperative-perception pipeline and measure how incorrect freshness decisions propagate to task output without adding a compensation network.
Independently recompute coverage, false-fresh, false-stale, uncertainty, overhead, and release hashes.
falsifiableClaims: Without clock-domain and synchronization evidence, observationally identical parameter worlds can have opposite one-way-age and deadline truth.
When valid synchronization intervals cover the true mappings, the age interval attains preregistered coverage and produces no false-fresh event outside that interval.
At least one frozen public path directly subtracts timestamps across unproven clock domains and changes freshness behavior under offset, drift, or relock with an otherwise fixed network process.
If every audited path proves a common time source and valid bounds, naive and oracle verdicts remain equivalent within those bounds.
metrics: Count of identical observations with opposite deadline truth
Optional frozen-model AP or trajectory difference
killCriteria: The frozen release cannot be parsed or event semantics cannot be assigned.
The counterexample changes payload, message order, or the network service process.
No calibrated truth is available for coverage validation.
The interval contract fails its preregistered coverage.
The observed discrepancy reduces to a parser bug.
Every target timestamp is proven to share one time basis with a valid uncertainty bound and no observationally equivalent counterexample remains.
claimGuardrails: A PTP configuration or deployment statement is not per-message timestamp provenance.
ROS Header, packet capture time, MCAP publish time, host receive time, and sensor capture time are not interchangeable.
Any result is limited to the named standard version, repository commit, dataset take, and timestamping plane.
